takeaway: Acute-phase proteins are made mainly in the liver in acute inflammation; examples are CRP, fibrinogen and serum amyloid A.

question.text: Which of the following is an acute-phase protein?

lines.text: In acute inflammation, the body raises certain proteins to fight the insult.
These acute-phase proteins are made mainly in the liver.
Fibrinogen is one of them. So are C-reactive protein, the most used in clinical practice, and serum amyloid A.
They can rise several hundred-fold above normal.
The interleukins and interferon gamma are signalling molecules, not acute-phase proteins, so they are crossed out.
